dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.summary: At-a-glance host health, open tasks, and shortcuts—the usual place to start daily checks.

features.name: Health summary
features.purpose: Key status for services, disk, protection mode, and more.

features.name: Quick links
features.purpose: Jump to common pages without hunting the menu.

features.name: Alerts and tasks
features.purpose: Items that need attention (updates, quotas, and similar).

useCases: Daily host health check
When something looks wrong, start here then drill into a subsystem
workflow: Open the related feature page for details
caveats: This is a summary view only—details and apply results are authoritative on each feature page

projects.title: Website projects
projects.summary: Manage document roots, runtimes, domains, and deploy lifecycle per site.

features.name: Project list
features.purpose: Create, search, and open each site.

features.name: OS user isolation
features.purpose: Optional dedicated Linux user and home per project.

features.name: Templates
features.purpose: Scaffold a new site from a preset template.

useCases: Host several sites on one machine
Separate system users for stronger isolation
caveats: Deleting a project affects files and services—back up first
published ≠ publicly resolvable; DNS must be correct

projectDetail.title: Project detail
projectDetail.summary: Control center for one site: deploy, env, health, backups, and network endpoints.

features.name: Deploy
features.purpose: Start or update the runtime for this site.

features.name: Environment
features.purpose: Edit project env vars safely.

features.name: Health and logs
features.purpose: Probe readiness and open related logs.

useCases: Ship a code change for one site
Rotate secrets without touching other projects
caveats: Apply / execute rules still apply—blocked means the host was not changed
Wrong env values can take the site down; change carefully

email.title: Mail
email.summary: Mail domains, mailboxes, and delivery settings, with DNS checklist guidance.
email.audience: Operators running self-hosted or business mail

features.name: Mail domains
features.purpose: Domains that send and receive mail.

features.name: DNS suggestions
features.purpose: MX / SPF / DKIM / DMARC records to publish.

features.name: Health and reputation
features.purpose: Delivery readiness checks (some items are external).

useCases: Stand up a new mail domain
Debug soft-fail / reject after DNS changes
workflow: Send a test and review health
caveats: PTR, port 25, and IP reputation often need the host or IP owner
The panel cannot replace an external DNS provider or delist you from blocklists

emailDomain.title: Mail domain detail
emailDomain.summary: Mailboxes, aliases, DKIM, forwarding, and health for a single mail domain.

features.name: Mailbox management
features.purpose: Create mailboxes, quotas, and passwords.

features.name: DNS / DKIM
features.purpose: Show keys and records that must be published.

features.name: Advanced policies
features.purpose: Forwarding, rate limits, anti-spam, and similar (as implemented).

useCases: Create staff mailboxes
Rotate DKIM or fix failing DNS checks
caveats: DNS propagation depends on TTL
If webmail SSO is enabled, set passwords and plugins separately

files.title: Files
files.summary: Browse, upload, download, and manage files inside authorized paths.
files.audience: Operators who edit site files directly

features.name: Directory browser
features.purpose: Navigate under allowlisted roots only.

features.name: Upload / download
features.purpose: Move site assets or backup archives.

features.name: Project shortcuts
features.purpose: Jump from a project into its home directory.

useCases: Fix a static asset without SSH
Pull a backup archive from the host
workflow: Pick an allowed root or project home
caveats: Only allowlisted paths—no arbitrary full-disk access
Deletes can take a site down; back up important files first

publicFiles.title: Public files
publicFiles.summary: Controlled public download area (for example release packages or static assets).
publicFiles.audience: Operators who need public download links

features.name: Public area management
features.purpose: Manage files reachable over HTTP.

features.name: Quota
features.purpose: Cap usage of the public area.

useCases: Publish customer download packages
Share non-sensitive assets
caveats: Never put private keys or customer personal data in the public area

ftp.title: FTP accounts
ftp.summary: Create FTP / SFTP login accounts bound to home directories.
ftp.audience: Operators granting upload access to contractors or clients

features.name: Account CRUD
features.purpose: Create, disable, and delete FTP users.

features.name: Home directory
features.purpose: Confine each account to a specified path.

useCases: Let designers upload static files
Temporary contractor accounts
workflow: Confirm the FTPS service is installed and running
Create an account and set the home directory
caveats: Plain FTP is insecure; prefer FTPS / SFTP
Accounts take effect only after a successful service apply

ftpService.title: FTPS service
ftpService.summary: Install and tune FTPS (for example vsftpd): lifecycle and passive-mode ports.

features.name: Install and start
features.purpose: One-click install banner for software deployment.

features.name: TLS / passive ports
features.purpose: Configure secure transfer and the PASV port range firewall needs.

useCases: Enable secure file transfer on a new host
caveats: Requires system-change permission
If PASV ports are blocked, listing may work while transfers fail

mysql.title: MySQL databases
mysql.summary: Manage local MySQL databases, users, and connection settings with honest status on what was truly written to the system.
mysql.audience: Operators and developers who need databases for sites and apps

features.name: Database CRUD
features.purpose: Create, list, and delete MySQL databases (schema).
features.how: After adding in the list, use Apply to system for the server to take effect.

features.name: Users and grants
features.purpose: Create database accounts and bind access rights.

features.name: Apply and status
features.purpose: Distinguish draft, written, applied, and blocked—avoids false success.

useCases: Provision an isolated MySQL database and account for a new website project
Rotate app passwords or reclaim databases for decommissioned sites
workflow: Confirm the service page has installed and started the database engine
Create database and user; bind permissions
Click Apply to system and check returned status
Put the connection string in the project environment variables
caveats: Panel success ≠ the app can connect—verify host, port, firewall, and account grants
Deleting a database is high risk; confirm no production dependency before apply

mysqlService.title: MySQL service
mysqlService.summary: Install, start, stop, and tune the MySQL service itself (not database contents)—prerequisite for the data page.

features.name: One-click install
features.purpose: Install MySQL packages on the host (needs system-change permission).
features.how: Use One-click install on the page banner; do not install the same stack elsewhere.

features.name: Start / stop / reload
features.purpose: Control the systemd unit and report real outcomes.

features.name: Connection probe
features.purpose: Check whether the port is reachable and the service is ready.

useCases: First-time MySQL on a new host
Restart the database service in a maintenance window and confirm recovery
workflow: One-click install and wait for the result panel
Start the service and confirm active
Create databases and users on the data page
caveats: Without EXECUTE, only plans/scripts are written—no real apt / systemctl
root and non-root capabilities differ; some actions are honestly marked blocked
